title: When We Go

beats.what: Boyd discovered in the barn, alive but in shock; creatures left him alive to watch Tian-Chen die
Sara delivers news of Tian-Chen's death to Kristi; Kristi's reaction opens the episode's grief arc
Victor's father (Henry) meets Tabitha on his doorstep; she shows Victor's lunchbox as proof
Donna confronts Boyd: she is angry at herself for believing they would go home
Kenny learns his mother is dead; dissolves in grief at the church
Boyd finds Kristi at the lake; Kristi recounts Tian-Chen's dying words -- 'take care of him'
Food announced: Kenny and team have found crops growing in patches around the lake
Henry believes Tabitha after she names other missing people; leads her to the basement of research
Boyd closes the episode resolving to catch one of the creatures; asks Kenny for help
Voice on the phone claims to be Thomas again; the loop re-opens at the very end

character_beats.beat: wants to move forward and maintain leadership; the hour forces him to absorb blame for Tian-Chen's death, sit with Kenny's grief, and acknowledge the game is rigged -- then pivots to an offensive plan as the only way to survive
wants to stay angry at the place, not the person; she redirects fury inward -- she is angry at herself for ever believing Boyd's promise of home
wants Henry to believe her so she can find a path back; faces repeated refusal and near-police intervention before Henry's own grief-logic tips him toward trust

key_lines.line: The game here is fucking rigged. No matter what hand you play, you lose.
key_lines.why: Donna's summary of the town's existential trap -- the hour's philosophical core

key_lines.line: She looked at me, and she did not take her eyes off me.
key_lines.why: Boyd's account of Tian-Chen's final moments; what the creatures made him watch

key_lines.line: No matter how bad it gets, we'll never have this day again.
key_lines.why: Tian-Chen's mantra, spoken in her memory; the episode's emotional anchor

key_lines.line: We're gonna catch one of these fucking things.
key_lines.why: Boyd's pivot from grief to offense -- the decision that drives Season 3 forward

open_loops: What is in Henry's basement that might help Tabitha understand the place?
Boyd survived the barn -- what does it mean that the creatures chose to keep him alive to watch?
What did Miranda paint, and what did she know that Henry has kept secret for decades?
Why does the voice on the phone keep claiming to be Thomas?

payoffs.what: Henry's wife Miranda had the same visions of children in a tower that Tabitha experienced -- the 'chosen' pattern is confirmed as recurring

contradiction.wants: to be the practical, unsentimental survivor who never pins hope on promises
contradiction.does: admits she was stupid enough to believe Boyd's promise of going home -- revealing that hardness was always performance, grief was always underneath

tone_notes: The episode's most distinctive stat is the 132-second silence from roughly 04:10 to 06:22 -- the longest dead-air stretch in the run, covering the immediate aftermath of Tian-Chen's body being discovered. Density never exceeds 158 words/min (minute 19) and the overall average of 74.6 words/min is the lowest of the five episodes, signaling an episode that breathes grief rather than action. The final density spike at minute 57 (122) is the Thomas-phone cliffhanger jolting back to tension.
